findings.title: upsampled_count is only defined on the discover dataset but is routed to errors too
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is added only to the discover function converter. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True for the `errors` dataset, and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` then rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count() as count` for that dataset. The errors dataset has its own function converter, which does not define `upsampled_count`, so queries against `errors` with allowlisted projects will fail with an unknown-function error instead of returning counts.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility is checked against the outer dataset, not the dataset actually being queried
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` passes the closed-over `dataset` (the request's original dataset) to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, while the query itself is run against `scoped_dataset`. In the dashboard discover-split path the query is routed to `discover` or `errors` via `split_dataset`/`scoped_dataset`, so the decision to upsample can be made for a different dataset than the one that executes the query, which can apply `sum(sample_weight)` to a dataset that doesn't match the check.

findings.title: Negated error filter also triggers upsampling
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` uses a substring check `"event.type:error" in query`. A query such as `!event.type:error` (which excludes errors) contains that substring, so it is treated as an error-focused query and gets `count()` rewritten to upsampled counts. The check should parse the query or at least reject negated forms.

findings.title: Rewritten column embeds an alias that the column parser may not accept
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` returns the literal string `"upsampled_count() as count"` as a y-axis/column. Y-axes and selected columns are normally parsed as function names, optionally with arguments and no inline `as` alias. Passing an alias inside the column string is not part of the documented column grammar, so the query may be rejected or the response key may not be `count` as the tests expect. The alias should be applied by the caller, not embedded in the string.

findings.title: Cache can serve stale eligibility and invalidation is never wired up
findings.body: The allowlist eligibility is cached for 60 seconds under a key that does not encode the allowlist, and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called anywhere in this PR. Changes to `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` will therefore not take effect for up to a minute, and the docstring claiming invalidation 'should be called when the allowlist changes' describes a mechanism that does not exist. Either wire invalidation into the option update path or remove the dead function and fix the docs.

findings.title: Upsampling applied without guarding against missing sample_weight
findings.body: The transform assumes every event in allowlisted projects has `sample_weight`, with no null handling. Events lacking the client sample rate (e.g. older SDKs or events that bypass the sampling context) will contribute NULL/0 to `sum(sample_weight)`, silently undercounting errors rather than falling back to a plain count. The comment explicitly disclaims the check, but the data model does not guarantee it.

findings.title: Helper silently swallows all exceptions
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps dictionary access and float conversion in bare `except Exception: pass`. Malformed test data will silently produce events without the expected `sample_rate`, causing tests to pass or fail for the wrong reason. It also runs for every event stored through `store_event`, changing the stored sample_rate for all tests, not just upsampling tests. It should be scoped and not swallow errors.

findings.title: Stray submodule-pointer file committed to repository root
findings.body: The PR adds a file named `sentry-repo` containing a commit hash of the base revision. This looks like an accidental artifact (a gitlink or local checkout marker) and does not belong in the repository. It should be removed from the change.

findings.title: Upsampled count assertions are not backed by stored sample_weight
findings.body: The allowlisted-project test expects `count == 10` per bucket from two events stored with `client_sample_rate` 0.1, but nothing in the test setup sets a `sample_weight` on those events, so the expected value depends on ingest-side behavior that is not asserted or documented here. Without an explicit sample_weight the upsampled sum would be 0 or NULL, making the assertion either unverifiable or wrong. The test also never exercises the `errors` dataset, which is where the missing `upsampled_count` function would fail.

findings.title: No tests for the cache path or the public entry point
findings.body: The unit tests cover only the private helpers `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query` and `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`. The public `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (including the cache hit/miss logic and the cached-False case) and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` are untested, and there is no test for the negated-query case above.

findings.title: Unrelated error message text changed
findings.body: The error message for topEvents below 1 changed from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is outside the scope of upsampling. Any client or test matching the old message will break and the change is not mentioned in the PR description.
